title: Global Retail Content Delivery and Security
business: Global e-commerce retailers serving customers across multiple continents.
problem: High latency for international users and vulnerability to volumetric web attacks targeting the origin server.
solution: Azure Front Door provides a global entry point that terminates SSL/TLS connections at the edge, accelerates HTTP traffic via the Microsoft global network, and integrates web application protection to filter malicious requests before they reach the backend.
steps: Provision an Azure Front Door profile and define the frontend hostnames.
Configure backend pools to include origin servers across different regions.
Define routing rules to map incoming traffic to the appropriate backend pools based on path patterns.
Enable Web Application Firewall (WAF) policies and associate them with the frontend endpoints to inspect incoming traffic.
outcome: Improved page load times for geographically distributed users and reduced exposure of origin infrastructure to direct internet threats.
limitation: The service introduces a single point of configuration for global traffic routing; misconfigured routing rules can lead to widespread service outages. Verification requires monitoring the health probes and backend response codes in the Azure portal.
